To find the true length of line $AB$:

1. **Coordinates / Given Positions:**
   * Distance between projectors $= 70\text{ mm}$.
   * Point $A$: $10\text{ mm}$ above HP ($h_A = 10$), $15\text{ mm}$ in front of VP ($d_A = 15$).
   * Point $B$: $50\text{ mm}$ above HP ($h_B = 50$), $40\text{ mm}$ in front of VP ($d_B = 40$).
2. **Differences in Heights and Departures:**
   * Difference in elevations ($\Delta h$) $= h_B - h_A = 50 - 10 = 40\text{ mm}$.
   * Difference in departures ($\Delta d$) $= d_B - d_A = 40 - 15 = 25\text{ mm}$.
   * Distance between end projectors ($\text{Dx}$) $= 70\text{ mm}$.
3. **True Length Calculation (Analytic Method):**
   $$\text{True Length} = \sqrt{(\text{Dx})^2 + (h_B - h_A)^2 + (d_B - d_A)^2}$$ 
   $$\text{True Length} = \sqrt{70^2 + 40^2 + 25^2}$$ 
   $$\text{True Length} = \sqrt{4900 + 1600 + 625} = \sqrt{7125} \approx 84.41\text{ mm}$$.
proTip: You can solve true length problems either graphically using loci/rotation methods or analytically using the 3D distance formula.
